sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – mixed Roman-Dutch civil law, English common law and customary law; corporate law codified in the Companies Act 71 of 2008
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FIC Act), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 56A (Beneficial Ownership Register) as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; South African Reserve Bank directives and FIC Guidance Notes 7 and 7A; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the director’s/UBO’s country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (with consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each director and UBO (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (with consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry of the shareholder’s jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (with consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the registered office lease or occupancy authority (South Africa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Landlord or registered agent (CIPC-recognized service provider)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only – no apostille required for locally issued documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory due diligence screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and material counterparties against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, FIC targeted financial sanctions lists, and global PEP databases. Continuous adverse-media and sanctions match monitoring is required; any confirmed match must be reported to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) within the prescribed statutory timeline and may trigger enhanced due diligence under section 20A of the FIC Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) – Form CoR 9.1 (Name Reservation) and CoR 9.2 (Name / Company Change)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed name may be expressed in any of the 11 official South African languages, but must be typed in Latin-script characters. Where a name contains words from a non-official language, a certified English translation and cognate explanation may be required. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names or protected marks, and must not contain offensive, obscene, or otherwise undesirable words.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may make a representation in writing to CIPC within 30 days of the rejection notice using the e-services dispute/objection workflow, applying for reconsideration of the decision under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. If the initial reservation expires, a fresh CoR 9.1 application must be submitted before the statutory six-month deadline to maintain priority. Court review is available in the High Court under section 11(5) read with section 160(4).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a non-licensed wholesale apparel distributor, provided the registered address is a physical street address within the Republic of South Africa (not a post office box) capable of receiving service of process; the virtual/registered office must be maintained by a CIPC-recognized local agent and lease/occupancy documentation must be available for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – assessed at under 10% annual probability for a compliant low-risk wholesaler; unannounced inspections may occur where CIPC, FIC, SARS, or customs authorities act on filing irregularities, AML red flags, or gold-trading / high-value goods triggers, but standard off-price garment trading at ISIC 4641 presents no elevated physical compliance risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name reservation and pre-clearance fee (CoR 9.1)
CIPC private company (Pty) Ltd incorporation registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff – CIPC registration fee for standard private company (R175.00)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation agent / company secretarial professional fee (preparation and electronic filing of incorporation documents)
Customized Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) drafting for off-price apparel wholesale activities
Notarization and apostille bundle for each foreign director / UBO / corporate shareholder document set (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary and competent apostille authority (e.g., Secretary of State / Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark plus official apostille fee per instrument (variable by source jurisdiction)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register initial filing preparation and submission to CIPC (section 56A)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing is nil-cost at CIPC; agent fee reflects market benchmark for UBO identification and filing preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address and service-of-process acceptance arrangement (first 6 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (R2,200–R2,800 per six-month period)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SARS tax registration facilitation – income tax, VAT, and PAYE (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SARS statutory registration is fee-free; agent fee reflects market benchmark of R800–R900

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2024, ss. 13-15 (incorporation), s. 19 (legal persona), s. 25 (registered office), s. 50 (share register) and s. 66 (board of directors); Companies Regulations 2011; read with the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 for FICA verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, Republic of South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up share capital applies to a (Pty) Ltd; share capital is fixed in the MOI and shares are allotted for the consideration approved by the board. No escrow account or paid-in capital deposit is required at formation. Distributions remain subject to the solvency and liquidity test under ss. 4 and 46 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of ZA_PTY_LTD as a private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, with authorized capital of 1,000 ordinary shares and initial allotment of 100 fully paid ordinary shares, be and is hereby ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be the physical address stated in the Notice of Incorporation; that the Memorandum of Incorporation be adopted; and that the appointment of the first directors, the financial director and the compliance officer be confirmed, each with power to act singly. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors open bank accounts, sign mandates, and take all statutory steps to register the company with CIPC, SARS, and licensing authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, Republic of South Africa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to CIPC eServices; submit Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of a Company Name) for the name ZA_PTY_LTD plus two alternative names; attach certified IDs and the applicant address proof for FICA screening; pay the prescribed name reservation fee of approximately ZAR 50. The CIPC reserves the approved name for one year.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 duly completed
Certified copy of ID or passport of each incorporator
Proof of residential or business address (bank statement or utility bill)
Signed authorisation or power of attorney where filing is made through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with a more distinctive name or obtain a written consent letter from the prior rights holder; alternatively, an appeal to the Companies Tribunal may be lodged within 20 business days under s. 160 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation: Notice of Incorporation and MOI Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices portal: Company Registration Module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) with the Memorandum of Incorporation declaring a private company limited by shares; state the registered physical address and first directors in the filing; indicate authorized and initial issued shares; pay the standard company registration fee of approximately ZAR 175. The CIPC verifies the filing against the name reservation and FICA records, then issues the Registration Certificate and a certified copy of the MOI.
required_dossiers: E-filed Form CoR 14.1
Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
CIPC name reservation approval letter
Certified ID or passport copies of incorporators and first directors
Consent letter from the owner of the registered office premises
FICA-compliant proof of address for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any CIPC query by resubmitting the defective item within 10 business days through the eServices rectification workflow; after registration, defective MOI provisions may be cured by filing an MOI amendment notice under s. 16 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (internal governance); CIPC eServices for director detail updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the first board resolution at the inaugural directors meeting; record the share allotment in the securities register; adopt the registered office; appoint the directors, financial director, company secretary if appointed, and compliance officer; open the minute book, share register, directors register and beneficial ownership register; file any subsequent director or officer change to CIPC where the incorporation filing is updated.
required_dossiers: Signed original of the First Board Resolution
Securities register or share allotment statement
MOI and CIPC Registration Certificate
Registered office address consent and lease abstract
Directors signed acceptances of office and declarations including solvency where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify any defective resolution by a subsequent written shareholders or directors resolution; ensure minutes and registers are kept at the registered office; director declarations for foreign residents must be notarized and apostilled before the banking mandate is executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration: Income Tax, VAT and PAYE Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on SARS eFiling using the CIPC registration number; complete the income tax registration to obtain the corporate income tax reference number; apply for VAT using Form VAT 101 whenever projected taxable turnover equals or exceeds ZAR 1 million per annum; register as an employer for PAYE, SDL and UIF once employees are engaged; link the company bank account to SARS using the bank confirmation letter for refund purposes.
required_dossiers: CIPC Registration Certificate
Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
Certified identity or passport copies of directors
SARS eFiling business registration form with company details
Bank confirmation letter for the company operating account
Projected turnover statement for VAT threshold determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS raises verification queries, resubmit certified supporting documents through a SARS branch and complete the eFiling verification workflow; a VAT number may be issued within 21 business days; any late-filing penalty may be remitted under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 via a formal objection or remission request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Filing and Continuing CIPC Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices portal: Beneficial Ownership Filing Module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the beneficial ownership register identifying every natural person who ultimately owns or controls the company; file the prescribed beneficial ownership return using CIPC Form CoR 33.1 within 10 business days of incorporation; file Form CoR 33.2 within 10 business days of any ownership change; set the financial year-end; schedule the annual return and authorised-person notice where applicable.
required_dossiers: Signed register of beneficial ownership
Form CoR 33.1 initial beneficial ownership notice
Supporting chain of ownership documentation (shareholder agreements, trust deeds, or holding structures)
Certified IDs of beneficial owners
Director and shareholder register extracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects the beneficial ownership filing for incomplete ultimate-owner disclosure, obtain the underlying transfer or ownership documents and resubmit; late administrative penalties can be objected to and remitted through the CIPC penalty-objection process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises Licensing, Fire Safety and Municipal Trading Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Fire Services; Municipal Planning and Licensing Department; Department of Employment and Labour (UIF and COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the zoning permission for wholesale and warehouse use of the premises; obtain a valid Certificate of Occupancy and electrical Certificate of Compliance; apply to the municipal fire department for the fire compliance certificate under the National Building Regulations SANS 10400 Part T; install extinguishers, emergency signage and evacuation routes; register the business as a trading tenant with the municipality; register as an employer for UIF using Form UI-19 and for COIDA using Form W.As.2 at the Department of Employment and Labour.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and zoning certificate
Certificate of Occupancy
Electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC)
Municipal fire compliance application and building floor plan
Fire equipment maintenance contracts for extinguishers and emergency lighting
UIF Form UI-19 and COIDA Form W.As.2
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate minor fire safety findings and request an immediate re-inspection; where zoning is silent on wholesale use, obtain special consent from the Municipal Planning Tribunal; if COIDA registration is delayed, request a provisional employer number online via the e-COIDA portal so that payroll administration can commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (https://www.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a fixed place of business or engaging in taxable activity in South Africa must register on SARS eFiling. The normal procedure is to file the VAT101 VAT registration application together with certified incorporation documents, proof of physical address, bank account details and director identification. SARS issues a unique income tax reference number and, upon satisfying the registration conditions, a VAT vendor registration number. A non-resident vendor may be required to appoint a representative taxpayer in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (South African resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on South African source income; no pass-through treatment for a (Pty) Ltd)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective pass-through regime exists in South Africa. A proprietary limited company is compulsorily treated as an entity-level taxpayer. Hybrid debt, hybrid equity and hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act are mandatory anti-avoidance measures, not elective. Limited elections are available in respect of controlled foreign company status and the application of certain double taxation relief mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration where taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period exceed or are likely to exceed this threshold); voluntary registration permitted where annual taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. VAT vendors must issue tax invoices satisfying the requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act and retain them for five years. SARS eFiling supports electronic VAT return submission and API-based data exchange for large businesses, but there is no mandatory government-run clearance API or fiscal control unit requirement for every VAT invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating on exports is available under section 11(1) of the VAT Act for goods supplied and exported from South Africa in the ordinary course of trade, provided the exporter or the recipient physically removes the goods from the South African customs controlled area within the prescribed period and retains sufficient documentary proof. Certain qualifying supplies of services to non-residents under section 11(2) may also be zero-rated if the services are not consumed or used in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) showing final exportation
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Proof of export from the port of loading or border post
Inward remittance certificate or bank advice evidencing payment receipt from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may deny the zero-rating and assess VAT at 15% if export documentation is incomplete or the export is not proven. Penalties include additional taxes of up to 200% of the assessed VAT under the VAT Act, understatement penalties, administrative penalties and interest. Fraudulent or reckless zero-rating claims may trigger criminal prosecution and cancellation of VAT vendor status, and retrospective clawback can extend to the full period subject to verification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CIPC form prescribed under s33 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's registration date; CIPC annual-return fee is turnover-bracketed from USD 5 (ZAR 100) to USD 110 (ZAR 2,000); USD 27 (ZAR 500) assumed for the ZAR 10-50 million turnover bracket.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company is flagged 'In Default' immediately after the 30-business-day window; CIPC issues a notice of failure to file; the company cannot file other transactions or obtain a good-standing certificate; after two consecutive years of non-filing, CIPC initiates administrative deregistration (strike-off) under s82(3), exposing directors to personal liability and requiring a reinstatement application with compounded fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register confirmation (filed with the Annual Return under the Companies Amendment Act 2024)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be confirmed at each Annual Return filing; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 business days after the change occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false confirmation is a criminal offense: a director or officer may be fined up to USD 54,000 (ZAR 1,000,000) or imprisoned for up to 10 years, and the company may be struck off; CIPC may also issue a compliance notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) approval and presentation to the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting (private company AFS are not filed with CIPC; presented to members at the AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 15 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once in every calendar year and within 15 months after the previous AGM; AFS must be approved by the board and presented at the AGM.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who knowingly present defective AFS commit an offense; CIPC may issue a compliance notice; non-compliance may lead to an administrative fine or court order compelling compliance, and may contribute to director disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit is mandatory where the Public Interest Score (PIS) is ≥ 350 points, or where the Memorandum of Incorporation requires it; a company with PIS 100-349 must obtain an independent review by a registered accountant (unless the company is owner-controlled and the AFS were independently compiled); a private company with PIS below 100 is generally exempt from audit and review. PIS is computed under Companies Regulation 26(2) with points for employees, third-party liabilities, security holders, and third-party income.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for private companies with PIS ≥ 350; IFRS for SMEs for private companies with PIS < 350; no South African Local GAAP exists — the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Financial Reporting Standards Council prescribe IFRS / IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Ownership Register must be filed with CIPC and reconfirmed at every Annual Return; any shareholding transfer or change of beneficial owner must be reported to CIPC within 10 business days; the register is confidential to third parties but must be produced on demand to the CIPC, the Financial Intelligence Centre, and other organs of state.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and Shareholder Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for earlier years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays or preferential CIT rate for this trade. Targeted reliefs: s 12B renewable-energy allowance 125% (projects brought into use 1 Mar 2023-28 Feb 2025); s 12C manufacturing-asset allowance 40% initial and 20% annual; s 11D approved R&D expenditure deduction at 150%; assessed-loss set-off capped at 80% of taxable income per annum (s 20ZA); no group relief absent s 45 intra-group transaction election or s 44 merger relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Assessed losses may be carried forward indefinitely; annual utilisation limited to 80% of taxable income; carryforward forfeited on trade cessation, liquidation, or where a change in ownership is effected predominantly to utilise the loss without a substantial continuation of the same trade.
